packs.title: Science, Art and Gardens
packs.promise: Explore Columbus through science, art, garden scenes and neighborhood discoveries.

q.s: Let a work’s colors start an original idea.
st: Choose an artwork in an open gallery and record its artist and title.
Notice two colors and how they sit together.
Make an original small sketch or written scene using that relationship.

q.t: A Scene That Changes with You
q.s: See how a planted composition changes as you move.
st: Choose an open path with a view of topiary figures.
Walk a short comfortable distance and stop in two clear places.
Compare which shapes overlap from each position.

q.s: Learn something from the choices on two current menus.
st: Visit during current merchant hours and keep queues clear.
Find two ingredients named on different menus and record the merchants.
Choose one ingredient you would like to learn to cook with.

packs.title: Brick by Brick
packs.promise: Look closely at village streets, pocket gardens and a park.

q.s: Collect the patterns under a neighborhood.
st: From a clear sidewalk, find one long horizontal line, one repeating joint and one edge where two surfaces meet.
Give each pattern a short name. Look at paving or outward-facing masonry without entering a front garden.
Record your three names or a close view that avoids house numbers and people.

q.s: Find the borders that make a street.
st: Find an edge made by paving, an edge made by planting and an edge made by a building or fence.
Observe only from the public sidewalk. A gap or empty planter can count as a planting edge.
List the three materials you noticed without collecting or touching anything.

q.s: Find three ways a path meets planting.
st: Stay on the open garden path and find a straight edge, a repeated paving shape and a change of texture.
Plants, mulch or an empty seasonal bed all work for the texture change.
Name your three finds without picking leaves or entering beds.
